name: Goat Meat (Raw)
imageAlt: fresh raw lean piece of goat meat on a dark rustic stone surface
description: Goat meat is an exceptionally lean, nutrient-dense red meat derived from Capra hircus. Valued worldwide for its subtle, wild flavor profile and high metabolic efficiency, it is one of the leanest domestic sources of structural protein. The meat is uniquely rich in intracellular minerals, lean structural lipids, and essential hematinic cofactors that support the cardiovascular system and musculoskeletal recovery.
macroIntro: Goat meat provides a superior, hyper-lean, protein-dominant macronutrient profile, offering significantly less saturated fat and total lipid mass compared to traditional commercial red meats.
microIntro: Goat meat possesses an elite, bioavailable micronutrient matrix, delivering massive concentrations of organic iron, metabolic potassium, and critical neuro-supportive B vitamins.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Noticeably low caloric density for red meat, maximizing protein delivery per calorie while maintaining a minimal systemic lipid load.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Outstanding concentration of high-quality complete protein, containing all nine essential amino acids in optimal proportions for myofibrillar repair and nitrogen retention.

macroNutrients.name: Fats
macroNutrients.description: Exceptionally lean lipid matrix characterized by remarkably low levels of saturated fat alongside a high relative concentration of monounsaturated fatty acids.

macroNutrients.name: Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: Contains zero carbohydrates or plant fiber, ensuring a complete absence of glycemic impact on plasma glucose dynamics.

microNutrients.name: Heme Iron
microNutrients.description: An exceptionally dense source of organic iron, surpassing the levels found in beef and chicken for maximum hemoglobin saturation.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
microNutrients.description: An indispensable cofactor required for myelin sheath maintenance, neural signal transmission, and erythropoiesis.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: An intracellular cation that helps maintain systemic osmotic equilibrium and regulates cardiac electrical activity.

microNutrients.name: Zinc
microNutrients.description: A bioavailable trace mineral serving as a structural anchor for DNA synthesis, testosterone production, and immune cascades.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
microNutrients.description: A key metabolic coenzyme (NAD/NADP) necessary for substrate oxidation and cellular energy release.

microNutrients.name: Selenium
microNutrients.description: An essential trace element incorporated into glutathione peroxidase, providing robust antioxidant protection.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
microNutrients.description: Accelerates amino acid metabolism, neurotransmitter synthesis, and supports healthy carbohydrate metabolism.

microNutrients.name: Phosphorus
microNutrients.description: Essential for bone mineralization, ATP energy storage, and maintaining cellular pH balance.

healthBenefits: Muscle Tissue Support: High protein-to-fat ratio accelerates nitrogen retention and preserves lean muscle mass.
Hematopoiesis: High levels of heme iron optimize erythrocyte maturation and aid in preventing anemia.
Vascular Health: Low saturated fat content helps maintain a healthy systemic lipid profile.
Fluid Balance: Potassium optimizes arterial tone and supports water-salt homeostasis.
Immune Defense: Bioavailable zinc supports cell replication and the body's natural defense mechanisms.
precautionsIntro: Purines, collagen density, and thermal processing: proper preparation maximizes health benefits.
precautions: Gout Considerations: Goat meat contains an elevated concentration of purines, which can trigger uric acid accumulation in individuals prone to gout.
Collagen Density: Due to the animal's active lifestyle, the meat is dense; slow, moist cooking methods are recommended to tenderize connective tissues.
AGE Compounds: Aggressive cooking techniques (high-heat grilling over open flames) generate harmful carcinogens (HCAs and PAHs).
